title: 02 — Calling Models in Practice
html:
02 — Calling Models in Practice

The one idea: every generative AI feature is built from a handful of API moves: send messages, stream the reply, ask for structured output, offer tools, cache the stable part of the prompt, and handle errors. Learn these once, and chatbots, agents and voice assistants are combinations of them.

1. What it is

A model API is an HTTPS endpoint. You send a list of messages (user and assistant turns), an optional system prompt, optional tools, and settings. You get back content blocks (text, tool calls, sometimes reasoning summaries) and usage (tokens in and out).

The examples use the Claude Messages API with the official Anthropic SDKs, in Python (pip install anthropic) and C# (dotnet add package Anthropic). Other providers have the same building blocks under different names. In .NET, Microsoft.Extensions.AI (IChatClient) gives one abstraction over many providers, and the Anthropic C# SDK supports it.

All code here is not run (no API key in the build environment). It follows the official SDK documentation as checked on 2026-10-27. The SDKs read the key from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, so never hard-code keys.

2. Why it matters

  • Streaming decides whether a chat feels instant or frozen.
  • Structured output decides whether the next step can trust the result.
  • Caching often cuts the cost of a repeated long prompt by large factors.
  • Error handling decides whether a 429 at peak time becomes a retry or an outage.

3. The moves

3.1 One request

import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()          # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or a saved login profile)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system="You are a concise assistant for mutual-fund operations staff.",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain the difference between a direct and a regular plan."}],
)
for block in response.content:          # content is a list of blocks: check the type
    if block.type == "text":
        print(block.text)
print(response.usage.input_tokens, response.usage.output_tokens)

The API is stateless. For a conversation, you send the whole history every time (03).

The same call in C#:

using Anthropic;
using Anthropic.Models.Messages;

AnthropicClient client = new();
var response = await client.Messages.Create(new MessageCreateParams
{
    Model = "claude-opus-5-5",
    MaxTokens = 16000,
    Messages = [new UserMessageParam { Content = "Explain the difference between a direct and a regular plan." }],
});
foreach (var text in response.Content.Select(b => b.Value).OfType<TextBlock>())
    Console.WriteLine(text.Text);

3.2 Streaming (for chat UIs and long outputs)

with client.messages.stream(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=64000,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Draft a one-page explainer on NAV."}],
) as stream:
    for text in stream.text_stream:
        print(text, end="", flush=True)   # forward each chunk to the browser (SSE or WebSocket)

3.3 Structured output (when code consumes the answer)

from pydantic import BaseModel

class FundFacts(BaseModel):
    scheme_name: str
    expense_ratio_pct: float
    plan: str

response = client.messages.parse(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Extract: 'Scheme X Direct Growth, TER 0.62%'"}],
    output_format=FundFacts,
)
facts = response.parsed_output           # a validated FundFacts instance

3.4 Tools (function calling)

You describe functions. The model asks to call them, and your code runs them. The SDK's tool runner drives the loop for you:

from anthropic import beta_tool

@beta_tool
def get_nav(isin: str, date: str) -> str:
    """Return the published NAV of a fund plan.

    Args:
        isin: The plan's ISIN.
        date: Date as YYYY-MM-DD.
    """
    return lookup_nav(isin, date)        # your code: a database or API call

runner = client.beta.messages.tool_runner(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    tools=[get_nav],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What was the NAV of INF000X01AB1 on 2026-10-23?"}],
)
for message in runner:                   # stops when the model stops calling tools
    print(message)

Rules worth knowing:

  • Return every tool result for a turn in one message.
  • Report a failing tool as a result with is_error: True, rather than dropping it.
  • Set strict: True on hand-written tool schemas (with additionalProperties: false) to guarantee valid arguments.
  • On the newest Claude models, forcing a specific tool with tool_choice returns an error. Steer from the prompt and keep strict instead.

3.5 Prompt caching (for long, repeated context)

response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"},      # cache the stable prefix automatically
    system=long_policy_document,              # e.g. 50 KB of rules, the same on every request
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}],
)
print(response.usage.cache_read_input_tokens)  # above zero on later calls = cache hits

Caching is a prefix match. Keep stable content first (system prompt, tool list), and put changing content (timestamps, the question) last. A timestamp inside the system prompt silently breaks it.

3.6 Errors and retries

The SDK already retries connection errors, 408, 409, 429 and 5xx with backoff (two retries by default). Catch the specific errors you can act on:

try:
    response = client.messages.create(model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=16000, messages=messages)
except anthropic.RateLimitError as e:
    retry_after = int(e.response.headers.get("retry-after", "60"))   # back off, or queue the request
except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
    if e.status_code >= 500:
        ...                                                          # transient: retry later
    else:
        raise                                                        # 4xx: fix the request

Also check response.stop_reason:

  • max_tokens means the answer was cut off.
  • refusal means the model declined.
  • tool_use means it wants a tool.

3.7 Cost levers, in order

  1. Cache stable prefixes.
  2. Trim history and retrieved text to what matters.
  3. Lower the reasoning effort for simple routes (output_config={"effort": "low"}).
  4. Use batch processing for offline jobs, which is cheaper and asynchronous.
  5. Use a smaller model tier, only where evaluation shows quality holds.

4. Working code

All code is in section 3, and not run here. To try it, create an API key in the Claude Console, export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and run each snippet.

5. Common mistakes

  1. Hard-coding API keys. Use environment variables or a vault (Azure Key Vault in production).
  2. Not streaming long answers. Users see nothing, and long requests can time out.
  3. Parsing free text when code needs fields. Use structured output.
  4. Breaking the cache with volatile content early in the prompt.
  5. Writing your own retry loop on top of the SDK's. Configure max_retries, and handle only what you can act on.

6. Exercise (1.5 hours, needs an API key)

  1. Run the single request, then the streaming version, and compare how they feel.
  2. Extract FundFacts from five made-up factsheet lines, and count how many parse.
  3. Send the same 5,000-word system prompt twice with caching on, and compare cache_read_input_tokens.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why must a chatbot resend the history?
  2. When should you stream?
  3. What guarantees that a tool's arguments match its schema?
  4. What silently breaks prompt caching?
  5. What does stop_reason == "max_tokens" tell you?

Answers

  1. The API is stateless. Each request contains everything the model sees.
  2. For chat interfaces and any long output, so users see progress and requests don't time out.
  3. strict: true on the tool definition, with additionalProperties: false and the required fields listed.
  4. Any change early in the prefix: a timestamp or ID in the system prompt, a reordered tool list, unsorted JSON.
  5. The answer was cut off at the token limit. Raise max_tokens or stream.
